findings.title: Stateful subclass leaves abstract methods unimplemented and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler, which declares abstract methods counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data. The subclass body is only pass, so it stays abstract. Detector.detector_handler does group_type.detector_handler(self), which will raise TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class for any detector with type metric_alert_fire. Previously it implemented evaluate returning [] and was instantiable. Consequence is a runtime crash in process_detectors instead of a no-op.

findings.title: get_state_data crashes with KeyError when detector defines no counters
findings.body: In get_state_data, counter_updates is initialized to {} and only populated inside if self.counter_names:. The final loop unconditionally builds DetectorStateData with counter_updates=counter_updates[gk]. When counter_names is empty list, the dict stays empty and the lookup raises KeyError for every group key. Consequence is evaluate crashes for any stateful detector that legitimately tracks zero counters, even though an empty list should be allowed.

findings.title: Stale docstring says evaluate returns a list
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate signature was changed to return dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], but its docstring still says it returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult with one result per group key. A reader or future handler author relying on the docstring will expect a list. Consequence is confusion and potential misuse of the new dict-keyed contract.

findings.title: Expected occurrence built with wrong group key causing fingerprint mismatch
findings.body: In TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe the expected occurrence is built via build_mock_occurrence_and_event with group_key val1, but evaluate_group_key_value is invoked with group_key group_key. The helper derives fingerprint via build_fingerprint(group_key), so expected fingerprint is <detector_id>:val1 while actual is <detector_id>:group_key. DetectorEvaluationResult equality includes the occurrence, so the test does not compare like-for-like. Consequence is the test is incorrect and does not validly verify the occurrence produced for group_key.

findings.title: Multi-group test uses wrong value and helper ignores value
findings.body: In TestProcessDetectors.test_state_results_multi_group the data packet has group_vals {group_1: 6, group_2: 10}, but the expected occurrence for group_2 is built with value 6. Moreover build_mock_occurrence_and_event never uses its value argument. The new hook build_occurrence_and_event_data receives value from evaluate_group_key_value, but no test verifies the correct per-group value reaches it. Consequence is a bug passing the wrong value to occurrence creation would not be caught.
